case: Failed InnoDB DML rolls back parent and transactional trigger rows; MyISAM, MEMORY and CSV trigger writes survive; AUTO_INCREMENT allocation remains consumed after rollback.
contract: A successful InnoDB insert seeds the parent and trigger-effect rows at ID 1.
The batch inserts ID 2, then fails on duplicate ID 1; both the parent row and its InnoDB trigger write for ID 2 roll back.
The AFTER INSERT effects for IDs 1 and 2 remain in MyISAM, MEMORY and CSV tables.
A separate failing InnoDB batch removes its inserted row but does not restore the AUTO_INCREMENT counter; the next successful insert receives ID 3.
This establishes only the named MySQL engine and side-effect cases; it does not establish rollback behavior for all engines or side effects.

focused_test.command: rtk proxy cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-mysql --test integration mysql_atomic::mysql_batch_rollback_does_not_claim_to_reverse_nontransactional_engine_effects -- --ignored --exact --test-threads=1

remaining: Other storage engines and side-effect patterns remain untested.
